segments.text: The Electronic Fund Transfer framework regulates electronic movement of money and the rights, duties and documentation associated with electronic payment systems.
Prepare the institutional side (payment systems and State Bank supervision) and transaction side (payment instruments, authorization, records, errors, liability and legal remedies).
Correct primary authority: Payment Systems and Electronic Fund Transfers Act, 2007 and current State Bank of Pakistan regulations.

The official federal statute is titled the Payment Systems and Electronic Fund Transfers Act, 2007. The shorter syllabus wording “Electronic Fund Transfer Act, 2007” should therefore be corrected in the teaching text while cross-referenced so the student recognizes the FPSC heading. Pakistan Code lists the 2007 Act under its full title.

The statute provides a legal framework for payment systems, electronic fund transfers, payment instruments, system operators and regulatory oversight. It is not merely a law about internet banking between two private parties.

Payment systems move funds through organized technical and institutional arrangements. A modern system may involve clearing, settlement, real-time gross settlement and designated operators. The State Bank of Pakistan’s supervisory role is therefore central to systemic reliability and financial stability.

Designation and revocation powers, operational standards and settlement rules should be understood as controls over infrastructure whose failure could affect many participants, not only one customer transaction.

Electronic transfers create evidentiary and consumer-protection questions: Was the transfer authorized? Was the instruction correctly executed? What records exist? Was an error reported within the required process? Which participant bears responsibility under the statute and applicable regulations?

A strong problem answer separates system-level regulation from customer-level liability and documents the chain: instruction → authentication → processing → clearing/settlement → account entry → notice/error resolution.

items.text: The Act deals with electronic movement of money through organized payment systems and defines rights and responsibilities of system operators, financial institutions and users.
At the system level, study designation, supervision, clearing and settlement arrangements. At the transaction level, study payment instruments, authorization, documentation and error handling.
Electronic records are essential because disputes may concern whether a transaction was authorized, when it occurred, what instructions were given and which institution bears responsibility.
Error notification and liability rules protect both system reliability and users. A good answer identifies the actor, duty, breach and remedy rather than describing electronic banking generally.

rows: Common confusion to avoid: Do not turn this topic into a general essay on digital banking. The syllabus asks for the legal framework of payment systems and fund transfers.

items.text: Learn who bears what duty at each stage of an electronic transfer.
Check current SBP law/regulations for contemporary detail.

segments.text: Electronic transfer requires reliable authorization and records.
Payment systems need operational and supervisory rules.
Error notification and allocation of liability protect system integrity and users.
